content_metadata.description: In-depth exploration of tight junctions and their role in cellular biology.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the transmembrane protein responsible for forming tight junctions?

qAndA.answer: They create a continuous, belt-like seal that separates different pumps, carriers, and receptors in the plasma membrane, effectively blocking the passage of substances.
qAndA.question: How do tight junctions prevent the exchange of materials between cells?

qAndA.answer: The intestine, where tight junctions prevent digested food from leaking into the bloodstream.
qAndA.question: What is one example of a body cavity sealed off by tight junctions?

qAndA.answer: The blood-brain barrier, which prevents harmful substances from entering the brain.
qAndA.question: What structure do tight junctions form in the brain?

qAndA.answer: They create an impermeable barrier that prevents urine leakage into the extracellular space.
qAndA.question: How do tight junctions in the urinary bladder benefit its function?

activities.description: Dr. Qureshi explains the structure and function of tight junctions, highlighting their role as a barrier that limits the diffusion of ions and solutes.
He further explains the belt-like adhesive seal nature of tight junctions and their ability to prevent the passage of water, ions, and large solutes between cells.
Dr. Qureshi discusses how tight junctions separate different pumps, carriers, and receptors in the plasma membrane, preventing the exchange of materials.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: In this lecture, I am going to discuss about tight junctions or septate junctions.
Main points of the lesson are discs, large and urexin, cladins, advantage of tight junctions.
Tied junctions are also known as septate junctions.
There is a trans-mimbrane protein that is called cladins.
Join the plasma membrane by layer of two cells to create a barrier.
That limits our boundary, the diffusion of ions and salutes between the cells.
Tight junctions is a belt-like adhesive seal that selectively limits the diffusion of water,
ions and large salutes between the epithelial cells.
This allows the epithelial cells to separate the interior of the body from external world.
As we know that plasma membrane has sodium potassium pump, calcium pump, carrier proteins
for transport of ions and molecules.
But tight junctions, this separates different pumps, carriers and receptors in the plasma
membrane.
So, there is no exchange of materials takes place through tight junctions.
Tight junctions are literally areas of tight connections between the membranes of adjacent
cells and these connections are so tight that no space remains between the cells and substances
cannot leak between them.
In russophila, the proteins include discs, large and urexin.
Tight junctions are unique to vertebrates and they contain a protein that is called
cladins.
Because of their ability to occlude, our block substances from passing between the cells,
this form of junction between the cells act as a wall within that issue and keeping the
molecules on one side.
Tight junctions, cells connected by tight junctions, seal of the body cavities.
For example, tight junctions between the cells lining the intestine prevent substances,
prevent digested food in the intestine from passing between the cells.
So, digested food directly entering the blood.
The sheet of cells does act as a selective barrier and food substances must be transported
across the plasma membranes through the intestinal cells and they enter into the bloodstream.
This arrangement helps to prevent toxins and unwanted materials from entering the blood
directly and also prevents nutrients from leaking out of the intestine.
Tight junctions are also present between the cells that line capillaries in the brain.
They form the blood brain barrier which prevents many substances in the blood from passing
into the brain.
The purpose of tight junction is to keep the liquid from escaping between the cells and
it allows a layer of cells to act as impermeable barrier.
For example, tight junctions which are present between the epithelial cells that lining
the urinary bladder, it prevent urine from leaking out into extra cellular space.
